tooltip.title: Treatment Types
tooltip.markdown: An overview of the alopecia treatment armamentarium, organized by mechanism or delivery method.

tooltip.title: Topical Growth Stimulants
tooltip.markdown: **Minoxidil (Rogaine):** The most well-known. Available OTC. Works by prolonging the anagen phase.

tooltip.title: Topical Anti-inflammatories
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Corticosteroids:** High-potency formulations (e.g., clobetasol) are used to suppress inflammation in scarring alopecias and alopecia areata.
-   **Calcineurin Inhibitors:** (Tacrolimus, Pimecrolimus) A steroid-sparing option for facial areas in FFA or DLE.

tooltip.title: Systemic Oral Therapies
tooltip.markdown: Pills taken by mouth to treat hair loss from within.

tooltip.title: Oral Growth Stimulants
tooltip.markdown: **Low-Dose Oral Minoxidil (LDOM):** A highly effective, increasingly popular off-label treatment for various alopecias, especially AGA.

tooltip.title: Anti-androgens
tooltip.markdown:
-   **5-alpha Reductase Inhibitors:** Finasteride and Dutasteride block the conversion of testosterone to DHT. Mainstay for male AGA.
-   **Androgen Receptor Blockers:** Spironolactone is used off-label in women with FPHL.

tooltip.title: Systemic Immunomodulators
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Hydroxychloroquine/Doxycycline:** Used for their anti-inflammatory properties in lymphocytic scarring alopecias like LPP and DLE.
-   **Methotrexate/Cyclosporine:** More potent immunosuppressants for severe cases.

tooltip.title: Targeted Biologic Therapy (JAK Inhibitors)
tooltip.markdown: **Baricitinib & Ritlecitinib:** FDA-approved oral medications that target the Janus kinase pathway, reversing the autoimmune attack in alopecia areata.

tooltip.title: Intralesional Corticosteroids
tooltip.markdown: Direct injection of steroids (e.g., triamcinolone) into the scalp skin. A first-line treatment for patchy AA and used to control inflammation in scarring alopecias.

tooltip.title: Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP)
tooltip.markdown: Involves drawing the patient blood, concentrating the platelets, and injecting the PRP into the scalp to stimulate growth.

tooltip.title: Low-Level Light Therapy (LLLT)
tooltip.markdown: Also known as photobiomodulation. Uses red light devices (caps, combs) to stimulate cellular activity in the follicles.

tooltip.title: Surgical Therapies
tooltip.markdown: The definitive option for restoring hair in stable areas of loss.

tooltip.title: Hair Transplantation
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Concept:** Moving DHT-resistant follicles from the occipital scalp to areas of thinning.
-   **FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction):** Individual follicular units are harvested, leaving minimal dot scars.
-   **FUT (Follicular Unit Transplantation):** A strip of scalp is removed, and follicles are dissected under a microscope.
